findings.hypothesis: An uninterrupted conversation grows attached message DOM, the messageNodes Map and the in-memory transcript without a count or character bound; the 60-message persistence limit does not limit the live panel.
findings.whyReachable: Production send pushes two messages and appendMessage adds two articles and map entries per exchange. Only New Chat clears these structures. Production send/receive/finish executed in a fake DOM/API fixture retained 200 messages, 200 map entries and 200 article nodes after 100 exchanges, versus 60 saved messages.
findings.expectedScope: Sustained AI conversations in one live panel only. Confirmed ownership/count growth, not a measured leak or physical memory size. Existing transcript is user-visible functionality; the text itself is not automatically disposable waste.
findings.risk: High if fixed by silently dropping old messages. Preserve transcript access, retry buttons, current streamed message, keyboard/assistive log behavior, scroll position and last-30 provider history. No blanket 60-message in-memory truncation without a product retention decision.
findings.cheapReproduction: node build/efficiency-20261103/extension-services-probe.mjs. Retention assertions execute production panel functions, replacing imports with stubs and stopping before event-registration/bootstrap code. No browser layout/GC/native transport is exercised.
findings.smallestFix: First bound rendered offscreen history with reversible transcript paging/windowing while preserving access to all conversation text. If bounding text is also desired, define explicit archival/retention behavior first. Avoid silently changing provider history. Independently replace repeated full-array find/filter work with current reply lookup/tail selection where behavior is identical.
relevantExistingTests: tests/ai/panel-browser.mjs (history, retry, New Chat, safe rendering; searched relevant assertions, not executed)
Need long-conversation fixture checking old-message access and scroll/focus before accepting a DOM window

findings.hypothesis: Each rendered streaming frame reparses all text received so far and replaces the complete reply subtree, so cumulative parse and allocation work grows with response length times rendered frame count.
findings.whyReachable: Production receive appends text then schedules renderDelta; its RAF invokes production renderMessage on the entire reply. With one 27-character line per synthetic frame, 100 frames produced a 2700-character final reply but parsed 136350 cumulative characters and created 10200 nodes.
findings.expectedScope: Active streaming replies, especially long formatted replies delivered over many frames. RAF already merges deltas arriving within one frame. This is operation/allocation count evidence using a synthetic DOM; it does not establish CPU time, paint cost, whole-browser RAM or battery gain.
findings.risk: Medium to high for incremental Markdown. A later chunk can close a code fence, complete inline syntax or change list grouping. Preserve final safe DOM output, chunk-boundary behavior, reduced motion, cancellation/error rendering and scroll anchoring. Simply delaying all rendering can regress responsiveness.
findings.cheapReproduction: node build/efficiency-20261103/extension-services-probe.mjs. Production renderer executed via vm and synthetic requestAnimationFrame queue; callbacks drained once per delta. No timing benchmark. Probe output records exact operation counts.
findings.smallestFix: Prototype committing complete stable blocks while reparsing only the unfinished tail, with a final full render for exact equivalence. Compare against current renderMessage across every chunk boundary before adopting. Alternatively evaluate a carefully bounded render cadence with explicit responsiveness acceptance; no current gain claimed.
relevantExistingTests: tests/ai/panel-browser.mjs safe HTML/link and streamed reply cases, not executed
Need differential DOM tests for split inline tokens, lists, quotes and open/closed code fences, plus real renderer scrolling acceptance

findings.hypothesis: Per-window conversation records may accumulate in in-memory storage.session after windows close; no repository cleanup path was found.
findings.whyReachable: Each window ID writes a distinct breezer-conversation-ID key. Search across features/ai and tests/ai found the key only in panel.js and no windows.onRemoved or storage.session.remove cleanup. Session lifetime/quota and actual window destruction behavior were not exercised.
findings.expectedScope: Repeated windows with AI conversations within one browser session, bounded by platform storage capacity. No cross-session persistent disk leak or exact memory amount established.
findings.risk: Cleaning on panel close would lose intended reopen history. A closed window cleanup must distinguish full window removal from temporarily hidden/closed side panel and avoid save/cleanup races.
findings.cheapReproduction: Next: disposable extension API fixture implementing storage.session merge semantics and windows.onRemoved; save conversations under several window IDs, remove windows and inspect exact keys. Then verify panel reopen within an existing window restores history and app-session restart behavior in an allowed disposable browser.
findings.smallestFix: If reproduced, remove only the exact per-window conversation key on confirmed window removal, with race-safe handling of final panel save. Do not clear on visibility change.
relevantExistingTests: tests/ai/panel-browser.mjs, existing conversation restore scenario; not executed
No dedicated per-window conversation cleanup test found by scoped search

excludedIdeas: Already verified page-context weak references, translation restore records, sidebar route pruning and native decoder: not new findings and outside this ownership.

Organato requests have explicit deadlines, owner cleanup and idle release. Update candidates intentionally retain their helper so verified candidates remain installable; do not drop checksum/signature identity state to save resources.
AI helper connection lifetime needs host-side evidence; this audit did not infer an idle native-process leak solely from the extension port.
Usage sampling alarms perform a requested feature. Disabling reporting, privacy checks, provider consent, security controls or features is excluded.

Panel input rebuilds a bounded settings select and shortcut popover rebuilds matching tabs. These are reachable small costs, but no measured user impact and no timing claim. Avoid caching unbounded tab data or imposing arbitrary result truncation.
Static release SVG/filter/shadow costs and eager theme workspace-store import are unmeasured. Preserve appearance until profiler evidence supports a change.
Document-lifetime event listeners in one-time panel/theme mounts are not evidence of cross-document leaks. Context/password mounts provide explicit disposal.
